sections.h2: Where is Socorro County and what is in it?
sections.html:
Socorro County is a large, thinly settled county in central New Mexico, with Socorro as its county seat. It was formed in 1852 and covers about 6,649 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 16,595 residents.

The county borders Cibola, Valencia, Torrance, Lincoln, Sierra and Catron counties. Interstate 25, U.S. 60 and U.S. 380 cross it. Its communities include Socorro, Magdalena, San Antonio, Lemitar, Polvadera and Veguita. Features in or near the county include the Rio Grande, Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge, the Very Large Array, the Trinity Site, New Mexico Tech and part of the Cibola National Forest.

For property tax, size matters. A parcel can be a lot in the city of Socorro, a small property along the river valley, or acreage far from a town, and the assessor values each by its own type and use.

sections.h2: What drives the Socorro County economy?
sections.html:
Government is the biggest piece of the Socorro County economy, and farming is a large share too. A 2020 New Mexico State University economic base study using 2018 data found these figures:

Measure (2018)Figure
County population16,735
City of Socorro population8,554
Government share of employment33.71%
State government jobs1,470
Farm employment822 jobs, 10.43% of employment
Accommodation and food services8.55% of employment

The city of Socorro lists the New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology, the Bureau of Land Management, Socorro General Hospital, the National Radio Astronomy Observatory, local government and Socorro Consolidated Schools among its major employers. New Mexico Tech was founded in 1889 as the New Mexico School of Mines.

With a county population of about 16,600 spread over thousands of square miles, a rural or vacant parcel may take longer to find a buyer than a house in the city of Socorro.

sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Socorro County?
sections.html:
Two elected offices handle property tax in Socorro County: the Assessor sets values and the Treasurer collects the money.

  • Assessor: PO Box J, 200 Church St, Socorro, NM 87801. Phone 575-835-0714. The office values homes, businesses and other taxable property and prepares the tax rolls for the Treasurer.
  • Treasurer: PO Box KK, 200 Church St, Socorro, NM 87801. Phone 575-835-1701. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the office is closed on federal holidays.
  • State Property Tax Division: Manuel Lujan Building, 1200 S. St. Francis Drive, Santa Fe, which takes over accounts that stay delinquent.

The county says it does not sell or broker real property and does not give advice on real property transactions, so use a title company or attorney for closing questions.

sections.h2: How is Socorro County property valued and how can you appeal?
sections.html:
The assessor mails Notices of Valuation to all owners by April 1, and the notice shows the value used to compute the tax. Taxable value is one-third of the appraised value, minus any allowable exemptions such as head of household or veteran exemptions.

An owner may protest the assessor's value or classification, the allocation of value to a taxing unit, a denial of an exemption, or a limit on a value increase. Under Section 7-38-24, as quoted in 2026 House Bill 285, the petition is filed with the county assessor, generally within 30 days after the notice is mailed. Where the notice was mailed with the prior year's tax bill, the deadline is the later of April 1 or 30 days after mailing.

HB 285 also amended the disabled veteran exemption. It sets the exemption at the veteran's federal disability percentage times taxable value, provided the veteran lives in the home as a principal residence. It also lets a veteran who sells or transfers a principal residence keep the exemption for the rest of the year or move it to a new home.

We did not confirm the dollar amount of the head of household exemption on the county site, so ask the Assessor for the current figure.

sections.h2: When are Socorro County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Socorro County mails tax bills on November 1, and taxes are due in two equal halves.

InstallmentDuePay by to avoid charges
First halfNovember 10December 10
Second halfApril 10May 10

When a deadline falls on a Sunday, it moves to the next business day. The Treasurer also offers prepayment options: four 25% installments on July 10, November 10, January 10 and May 10, or ten monthly installments from June 1 to March 1.

You can pay in person, by phone at 575-835-1701, online with a card or e-check, or by mail to PO Box KK. The Treasurer warns never to mail cash. If you have not received a bill by November 15, call 575-835-0714, because state law makes the owner responsible even without a bill.

sections.h2: What happens if you sell a Socorro County property with tax still due?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax does not disappear when a house is sold, so the closing needs to account for it. New Mexico taxes are a lien from January 1 of the tax year, as other county assessors in the state explain, and the title company will look for open balances.

The delinquency path is set by state law, and Socorro County's Treasurer describes it this way:

  • Each June the county mails a delinquency notice for any bill 30 or more days late.
  • If real property tax, penalty and interest remain unpaid two years from the delinquency date, the property can be sold at a state public auction.
  • Owners of mobile homes and personal property face seizure and sale after six months.
  • Owners of three or more years of back taxes will have the property sold by the State unless all years are paid before the sale.
  • An owner who cannot pay in full can ask the State Property Tax Division for an installment agreement to stop a sale.

The county posted a notice for a public auction on October 1, 2024, at 10:00 a.m. at 200 Church St in Socorro. The State publishes the sale lists in a newspaper for three weeks before each sale.

sections.h2: What options does a Socorro County owner have for selling?
sections.html:
An owner with a tax problem or an unwanted property can list it, sell it directly, or accept a cash offer.

  • List with an agent: works best when the house is in good shape and you have time.
  • Sell directly: avoids a commission but leaves paperwork to you.
  • Cash offer: from a buyer who purchases as-is, which can help when taxes are behind or the home is in a remote location. Ask for the offer in writing.

If you inherited property in Socorro County, the Assessor's records follow recorded documents, so deeds and death certificates must be recorded with the county clerk before ownership shows up on the tax roll. Before any sale, gather your tax bills, proof of payment, and any delinquency letters. Ask the title company to confirm what is owed at closing.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Socorro County?
faqs.a: Socorro is the county seat. The city had 8,707 residents in the 2020 census, and the county had 16,595.

faqs.q: When are Socorro County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and must be paid by December 10. The second half is due April 10 and must be paid by May 10. Bills are mailed November 1.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Socorro County property value?
faqs.a: File a petition with the county assessor, generally within 30 days after the Notice of Valuation is mailed. Notices are due by April 1. Call 575-835-0714 for the form.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Socorro County property tax?
faqs.a: The county mails a delinquency notice in June. If real property taxes, penalty and interest are unpaid for two years, the property can be sold at a state public auction.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Socorro County that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the balance is settled at closing. A title company will find the open amount and pay it from proceeds, and a cash buyer can also handle that step.
